tier_reason: Upgraded from C: the SIGMOD'24 paper's technical report, recovered from the repo history (technical_report.pdf at commit c5ea4ef), benchmarks LeCo against FOR, Elias-Fano, Delta and rANS on a stated Intel Xeon Platinum 8369B with public benchmark code (benchmark/fix_int, benchmark/auto_int) and -O3 -march=native in CMakeLists.txt; the compiler is never named, so not A.

corrections.baseline: Frame of Reference (FOR), Delta encoding (fixed and variable partitions), Elias-Fano (thirdparty succinct) and rANS, all built inside the repo; Parquet default encoding and RocksDB default index blocks in the system experiments
corrections.claimed_speedup: Technical report (SIGMOD'24 version): on nine integer data sets LeCo 'achieves a Pareto improvement'; versus FOR and Elias-Fano it improves compression ratio by up to 81% with comparable decompression and random-access speed; versus Delta encoding it is 'an order of magnitude faster in random access' with competitive or better ratio. In Parquet, a filter-scan query runs up to 3.9x faster and bitmap-scan up to 12.6x (up to 5.6x versus FOR); RocksDB throughput rises 16%. Compression throughput (Table 1, GB/s): FOR 0.81, Elias-Fano 0.58, Delta-fix 1.04, Delta-var 0.04, LeCo-fix 0.78, LeCo-var 0.02.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O3 -march=native, C++17, CMake Release build (CMakeLists.txt); compiler not named (README requires Ubuntu 20.04.4 LTS)
corrections.hardware: Intel Xeon (Ice Lake) Platinum 8369B @ 2.70GHz, 32GB DRAM, single thread (microbenchmark); 4x Xeon Platinum 8269CY @ 2.50GHz for the system experiments
corrections.caveats: No license file in the repo (usability reference). Baselines are FOR, Delta, Elias-Fano and rANS implemented or vendored inside the repo, not FastPFor, simdcomp or Simple8b. The main win is compression ratio at comparable decode speed, plus random-access speed over Delta; LeCo-fix compression throughput is slightly below FOR (0.78 vs 0.81 GB/s) and LeCo-var is about 40x slower to compress than FOR (0.02 GB/s). Numbers come from the technical report that was deleted from the repo on 2023-12-22 (commit 15d679e) and read from history; the published SIGMOD version was not opened (ACM and arXiv blocked). Compiler not named.

notes: Tier raised to B from a peer-reviewed paper version found in the repo's git history. Metadata matches: 17 stars, 3 forks, no license, last commit 2024-03-26 (stale). The Parquet 3.9x and RocksDB 16% claims are end-to-end system results, not the integer microbenchmark.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed DaMoN 2024 paper whose abstract (seen only as consistent search snippets of arXiv 2403.06898 and the ACM page) claims up to 2x faster LEB128 decoding than Folly and Protobuf; the paper body, hardware and methodology could not be opened here, and no code was found, so it stays at C rather than B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Abstract (search snippets only; arXiv blocked): about 500 lines of code achieve 'up to a 2x increase in decoding speed' compared with varint decoding in Facebook Folly and Google Protobuf; handles 32-bit and 64-bit unsigned integers with one C++ template using BMI2 PDEP/PEXT.
corrections.stars_or_usage: DaMoN 2024 workshop paper (ACM DOI 10.1145/3662010.3663439, arXiv 2403.06898); authors Gang Liao (University of Maryland) with Ye Liu, Yonghua Ding, Le Cai and Jianjun Chen (ByteDance)
corrections.caveats: Snippet only: arXiv (EGRESS_BLOCKED), ACM and a review site (themoonlight.io, EGRESS_BLOCKED) could not be opened, so the numbers, hardware and methodology are unchecked; the 'Intel m6i instances' hardware in the record did not appear in any snippet I saw. No public code found: the first author's GitHub account (gangliao, 68 repos) has no repository matching varint. Folly itself has a BMI2 (PDEP) varint commit, so the baseline may already use similar tricks for encoding.

notes: Paper and venue confirmed via search results; code not found and paper unreadable here. Candidate for a paper-access retier to B when arXiv is reachable. Left hardware uncorrected since I could not check it.
